theories.claim: TUI 'Read-only QA completed' banner is rendered as a product verdict promotion (e.g., 'QA passed' / pass verdict) rather than a neutral compatibility-status notice
theories.basis: Follow-up concern that the completed-state header in the bounded QA projection could be conflated with Conformance Review verdict promotion despite neutrality intent; banner is unconditional header when qa.Phase == "completed"
theories.verification_surface: internal/tui/qa_view.go:16-18 renderSprintQAView() branch, internal/tui/views.go:371-373 renderRouteSummary() QA delegation, and downstream Render() framing
theories.confirmation_condition: Render output for Phase==completed contains verdict-promotion language such as 'QA passed', 'QA succeeded', 'pass', or assessment-with-findings conflated into banner, or docs define completed as a verdict
theories.refutation_condition: Banner text is exactly 'Read-only QA completed (compatibility status); evidence-producing QA uses isolated writable copies' with no pass/fail lexing, Conformance Review verdict rendered separately as independent field 'Conformance Review: status=... verdict=... fresh=...', and dedicated tests assert absence of 'QA passed' while docs explicitly define 'QA completed means bounded work ended, not QA passed'
theories.inconclusive_condition: No direct operator comprehension study; semantic misread risk outside static code/text cannot be measured from code alone
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only inspection of qa_view.go, qa_view_test.go, model_test.go and documentation; reuse existing negative-assertion tests; no runtime mutation, no writable QA execution, no new checks

theories.outcome_reason: Static evidence refutes promotion: qa_view.go:17 emits only the neutral string 'Read-only QA completed (compatibility status); evidence-producing QA uses isolated writable copies' gated on Phase==completed, never on Assessment/IssueCount/Verdict; Conformance Review verdict remains a separate line 'Conformance Review: status=%s verdict=%s fresh=%t' (qa_view.go:21); qa_view_test.go:26-33 and model_test.go:138-145 explicitly assert presence of 'Read-only QA completed' and absence of 'QA passed' / 'Issues' promotion; docs/user-guide.md:357, docs/cli-reference.md:361, docs/architecture.md:153 and docs/phase3-json-schemas.md:33 define completed ≠ pass verdict and that QA cannot change Conformance Review verdict

theories.claim: Header position and wording still allow operator to conflate QA completed with Conformance Review pass despite literal neutrality
theories.basis: Banner is first line of QA view (preceding Phase/Fresh/Conformance Review lines) with parenthetical '(compatibility status)' that may be overlooked; concern notes residual UX misread risk even if text is technically neutral
theories.verification_surface: internal/tui/qa_view.go:16-22 ordering, internal/tui/views.go:371-373 summary ordering, internal/tui/model_test.go and internal/tui/qa_view_test.go render assertions
theories.confirmation_condition: Usability evidence or layout review showing operators skip parenthetical or read top banner as overall sprint verdict without inspecting the subsequent 'Conformance Review: status=... verdict=...' line
theories.refutation_condition: Layout or copy review demonstrates banner cannot be read as verdict because qualifier is on same line, Phase and Conformance Review are rendered immediately below, and no color/icon promotion occurs
theories.inconclusive_condition: No operator study, telemetry, or visual-hierarchy test in assigned context_paths; static code review can confirm literal text but not perceptual misread rate
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only rendering inspection and doc review only; do not invent user study or run interactive TUI; note bounded follow-up nature

theories.outcome_reason: Literal promotion is refuted (theory 1), but perceptual risk is inherently non-code: banner is correctly neutral and tested, docs consistently state 'QA completed means all admitted bounded work ended, not QA passed, and it cannot upgrade a failed or blocked Conformance Review' (user-guide.md:357, cli-reference.md:361). No evidence of promotion language exists, yet without human-factors data the residual possibility that an operator glances at first line and ignores '(compatibility status)' cannot be confirmed or refuted from file inspection alone. No fix required in read-only context; risk remains documentation/UX footnote, not a verdict-promotion bug.
